components.name: Snackbar
components.description:
Snackbar — transient feedback notification.

When to show (Save & error handling pattern):
• Success: "Your changes have been saved" — shown after all save requests succeed. Exit edit mode after display.
• Error (partial failure): "Some [entity] details couldn't be saved. Please fix the errors below." — shown when one or more models fail to save. Keep failed fields in Error state, apply Entered styling to saved fields.
• Never show a success snackbar if any part of the save failed.

Copy guidelines:
• Success: "Your changes have been saved."
• Partial error: "Some client details couldn't be saved. Please fix the errors below."
• Field-level error: "Email format is invalid." (field error, not snackbar)
• Keep messaging actionable — tell the user what to do next.

Placement: bottom of the screen, above sticky footer if present. Auto-dismiss after ~4s. Provide a manual dismiss option.

components.name: Tabs/ components
components.description:
Tabs.

Spacing: 12px between tabs.

Navigation IA:
• Tabs represent operational scope within a section.
• Tab labels are nouns (acceptable for navigational elements): "Overview", "Bookings", "Settings".
• Avoid duplicating top-level navigation patterns inside tabs — tabs are for sub-sections only.

Sentence case. Use "and" not "&".

components.name: badge - outline inverted
components.description:
Badge — status indicator.

Color semantics (Smily DS):
• 🟢 Green = Completed, Success.
• 🔵 Blue = Upcoming, Scheduled, Partially collected.
• 🟡 Yellow = Pending, Warning (may or may not be received).
• 🔴 Red = Danger, Take action required, Overdue.
• 🔘 Grey = Incomplete, Inactive, Expected but not confirmed.
• 🟣 Purple = Secured (guaranteed), or AI-powered feature.

Apply the color that matches the semantic meaning of the status — never use color for decoration.

components.description:
Breadcrumb navigation.

Navigation IA:
• Shows user's location within the application hierarchy.
• Breadcrumbs represent operational scope — each level reflects where settings or data "live".
• System-level: account → channel → rental → booking (most specific).
• Help users navigate between inherited settings levels without losing context.

Labels: sentence case, nouns acceptable (navigational element). Use "and" not "&".

components.name: Modal Date Picker
components.description:
Dialog (modal). Use for high-focus interruptions that require user action before proceeding.

When to use:
• Confirmations: "Are you sure you want to delete this?"
• Critical alerts: errors, destructive action warnings.
• Short forms or quick inputs.

When NOT to use:
• Showing item detail → Sidebar instead.
• Filtering/sorting → Sidebar instead.
• Complex multi-step workflows → Full page instead.

Save & error handling:
• Partial failure: keep failed fields in Error state, apply Entered styling to saved fields, show error snackbar.
• Full success: show success snackbar ("Your changes have been saved"), exit edit mode.
• Never reset valid inputs after failure. Scroll to first error on long forms.

CTA: action verb + object. "Save changes", "Delete booking" — not "OK" or "Submit".

components.name: Button - Solid
components.description:
Button usage guidelines.

CTA copy rules:
• Always use verb + object: "Create rental", "Save changes", "Send invitation", "Delete booking".
• Never use nouns alone: "New rental" → use "Create rental" instead.
• Nouns are acceptable only for tabs, nav items, and filter chips (navigation, not action).
• Always use "and" not "&". Sentence case only.

Icon placement:
• Left of text (default) — matches reading flow, reinforces hierarchy.
• Right of text — for directional/forward actions (Next →, More options ▾).
• Icon-only — only when space is limited AND icon is universally understood (trash, add, edit, settings).

Spacing: icon ↔ text = 4px. Icon size = 20px. Buttons or tabs = 12px gap. Between components = 16px.

components.name: row
components.description:
Table row.

Clickable cells in tables:
• If the row itself is NOT clickable (action button at row end), it is acceptable to have clickable cells within the row.
• If a row has a trailing action button, this provides a consistent interaction pattern and maintains accessibility.
• Key principle: action buttons at row end ensure consistent experience and clearly separate navigation from data content.
• Avoid having both a clickable row AND clickable cells — pick one interaction model per table.

Accessibility: having action buttons at the end of rows (not inline within cells) ensures screen readers can identify interactive elements reliably.

components.name: Filters and search desktop NEW
components.description:
Filter Bar — Desktop
Standardized filter bar for all list and calendar pages. Use this component set as the single source of truth for filter bar layouts on desktop.

LAYOUT RULES
• Elements are always top-aligned (prevents misalignment when horizontal scroll is triggered on narrow viewports)
• ≤3 filter buttons: show inline as pills
• ≥4 filter buttons: hide overflow behind a dropdown / "Filters" button

ICON
• Filter trigger uses the Font Awesome 6 funnel icon for consistent scaling

CLEAR FILTERS
• The "Clear filters" / "Clear all" action is a secondary text button — not red/destructive. It should not compete visually with primary actions.

ACTIVE STATE NOTE (known issue — separate ticket)
• When filters are active, the Filters button changes from outline to tonal (filled teal). This outline→tonal transition is inconsistent with other button patterns and will be addressed in a dedicated redesign ticket. Do not introduce custom workarounds in the meantime.

RELATED COMPONENTS
• Search Input / AI — for hover placeholder and focus interaction states
• Filter trigger icon: Font Awesome 6 "filter" (funnel)

components.name: Button - Text
components.description:
Text button (link-style). Secondary action, visually subordinate to primary CTA.

Color — always match the surface, not the sentiment:
• Positive (teal) — default, white/neutral backgrounds. Most common (73 instances).
• Informational (blue) — inside informational banners/cards (blue-50 background).
• Secondary (gray) — muted surfaces only, use sparingly (3 instances).
• Warning (red) — destructive/irreversible actions only. Never on neutral surfaces (5 instances).

Two sub-patterns:
• Navigation — trailing edit/pencil icon. Takes user to a related management screen.
• Expand/collapse — trailing chevron-down icon. Reveals inline detail without navigating away.

Placement: right-aligned in form section, vertically centered next to the relevant field group.

components.name: Input fields
components.description:
Input field.

States: Enabled placeholder → Hover → Focused → Entered → Error → Disabled → Locked (numeric).
Types: text, search, select, numeric. Sizes: large (85px), small (77px).

Error state (Save & error handling):
• On partial save failure: keep failed fields in Error state; apply Entered styling to successfully saved fields.
• Never reset valid inputs after failure. Show error snackbar alongside field errors.
• Error copy: specific and actionable — "Email format is invalid", not generic "Error occurred".

Scroll bar (desktop): always include in designs. Use Chrome/Firefox behavior as reference (scroll bar adds padding). Mobile: no reserved padding — bar sits on top of margins.

Spacing: between components = 16px. Between buttons/tabs = 12px.
Copy: use "and" not "&". Sentence case. Labels are nouns, helper text is a short sentence.
